verification: DOM-only: JSDOM event, semantic class, raw serialization and node identity checks; real browser visual rendering, native pointer behavior and Windows integration not verified

checks.name: Initial duplicates annotate every member independently in original, preview and editing rows
Editing second A to B keeps original A x2 and marks both live B members x2
Deleting one A preserves original duplicates but excludes preview deletion ghost from live counts
Deleting changed duplicate does not count the ghost old value or the removed new value
Adding a duplicate marks existing and new members, then changing it back removes stale marks
Raw equality keeps A, a, leading/trailing whitespace, slash and case variants distinct
Repeated empty segments are real duplicate members and trailing empty values survive application
Whole special strings retain semicolons without internal duplicate warnings
Moving, replacing, adding and removing retain all four semantic inline token states
Original pointer hover distinguishes equal-valued elements by stable ID
Preview pointer hover is symmetric with original hover and row hover
Token child-to-child pointer transitions preserve hover without highlight flicker
Input focus links all representations; hover overrides focus and leaving restores focused ID
Programmatic token focus links both sides without adding tokens to normal Tab order
Typing and row redraw preserve focused identity highlighting
Hover changes classes only: node identity, comparison content and serialization remain untouched
Deletion clears deleted hover identity, focuses remaining row and does not leave ghost highlight
Restoring resets duplicate annotations and clears hover of removed added identities
Close and cancel dismiss highlights; reopening starts without previous hover or focused IDs
Applying duplicate edits dismisses all highlight state while preserving raw output
Element feedback workflows emit no JSDOM runtime errors
